title: Design Ops: contribution guardrails, RFC staging, and component deprecation cadence
creator: Maya Rivera
description: Motivation: As our component library grows (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) we need a clear, lightweight governance layer so contributors (Design, Product, Eng) can ship changes safely and consumers can migrate smoothly. This ticket collects a single source of guidance for: 1) contribution guardrails and submission flow for new/updated tokens and components; 2) an RFC staging and signoff workflow tailored to UI primitives and token changes; 3) a predictable deprecation cadence and migration policy (including telemetry, aliasing, and changelog practices). The output should be: a consolidated contribution doc, a short review checklist that can be embedded in PR templates, an RFC staging page, and a deprecation playbook with example migration steps for token renames, button API removals, and chart props changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Contribution guide published in Confluence and linked from repository README.
- PR template updated to include the new Review Checklist items.
- RFC staging doc created with clear reviewers and expected timelines.
- Deprecation policy drafted with concrete timing (deprecation notice, sunset), example migration steps for tokens/buttons/tables/charts, and a telemetry plan.
- Two pilot PRs follow the process (one token rename, one small button variant change) and pass signoff.
notes: Focus on pragmatic defaults: require RFCs for public API or token namespace changes, lightweight design review for visual tweaks, and automated tooling for token aliases and codemods where possible. Keep the contributor experience friction minimal for small UX fixes.
review_checklist:
- Visual: matches design spec / screenshot provided.
- Accessibility: keyboard focus states, aria attributes, color contrast verified.
- Tokens: any token change must include token mapping (old->new) and fallback alias.
- API/props: breaking changes require RFC and migration example.
- Docs: storybook examples updated and MDX doc added.
- Performance: identify render cost for tables/charts and note expected impact.
- Test: unit tests + story snapshots + integration smoke where relevant.
- Telemetry: flag added for usage of old API/token for 90-day deprecation window.
- Rollout plan: feature flag/canary or small-scope rollout for high-risk changes.
rfc_process:
- Triage: contributor files a short intent RFC (1-2 paragraphs) in the RFC tracker.
- Stakeholders: add Design System stewards, Runtime/Serving UI (if performance-related), and PMs.
- Review window: 7 business days for non-breaking changes, 14 business days for breaking/public API changes.
- Signoff: requires at least one Design steward and one Eng reviewer. For token/visual changes affecting client apps, add an additional PM reviewer.
- Implementation: attach PR(s) to the RFC; merge only after signoff and after automated checks (storybook, lint, unit tests) pass.
- Post-merge: publish changelog entry and create deprecation notice if applicable.
deprecation_policy:
- Notice period: default 90 days from deprecation announcement for UI tokens and minor API changes; 180 days for removals of core button APIs or charting primitives.
- Communication: published in changelog, design-system Slack channel, and email to internal consumers.
- Aliasing: prefer alias tokens (oldToken -> newToken) for first 90 days and emit console warnings in dev builds.
- Codemods: for non-trivial renames, author a codemod and include migration instructions in PR description.
- Telemetry: enable usage counters for deprecated items; if usage remains >5% at sunset, escalate to Product for hold/extension.
- Emergency rollback: allow rollback for regressions with a patch release within 72 hours and a postmortem.
- Sunset: record final removal date and link to migration guide.
- Exceptions: changes required for security or accessibility regressions may have accelerated timelines.
